title: WHAT IS THAT IN YOUR HAND?

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to him, "What is that in your hand?" "A staff," he replied. The Lord said, "Throw it on the ground." Moses threw it on the ground and it became a snake, and he ran from it." - Exodus 4:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's question is beautifully simple. Not "what do you wish you had?" but "what is that in your hand?"

It was a shepherd's staff. A stick. The tool of a job Moses considered beneath him, a daily reminder of forty forgotten years. And God chose that ordinary object to become the instrument of a nation's deliverance.

We spend a lot of time telling God what we lack. God tends to ask about what we already hold. A skill. A home. A trade. A little time. A willingness to cook, to listen, to teach, to drive someone somewhere. Small things in surrendered hands become useful in ways we never planned.

But notice — the staff had to be thrown down before it became anything else. Surrender comes before usefulness. And when Moses let go of it, the thing became frightening.

Sometimes what God asks us to release feels dangerous. Pick it up again at His word, and you will find He has made it into something greater.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God already placed in my hand that I have dismissed as ordinary?
2. What am I unwilling to throw down and surrender to Him?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, here is what I have — it is not much. I throw it down before You. Take it and use it as You please. Amen.
